summary:
AstroHealth is an astronaut health monitoring application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It provides a centralised dashboard to monitor important health indicators, including heart rate, oxygen saturation, body temperature, sleep duration, exercise activity and radiation exposure.

The application uses changing simulated health data to display health conditions as Normal, Warning or Critical. It generates alerts when readings cross defined thresholds and provides suggested actions to help astronauts recognise potential health concerns. It also includes mission-time tracking, health trends, spaceflight risk monitoring and countermeasure guidance.

AstroHealth addresses the challenges of long-duration space missions, where radiation, altered gravity, isolation and distance from Earth can affect astronaut health. By bringing multiple health indicators and spaceflight risks together in one platform, it supports health awareness and self-monitoring, helping astronauts make informed decisions when immediate medical assistance is limited.
details: AstroHealth is an Android-based astronaut health-monitoring application designed to support health awareness during long-duration space missions. It brings important health indicators and spaceflight-related risks together in a single dashboard. The application displays health parameters such as heart rate, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, sleep duration, exercise time and daily radiation exposure. It uses changing simulated readings to represent an astronaut's health data over time. Based on predefined thresholds, the application classifies readings as Normal, Warning or Critical and generates alerts when a parameter reaches a concerning level. It also provides suggested countermeasures, health trends, telemetry history, mission-time tracking and a mission schedule. A dedicated risk-monitoring section highlights challenges such as space radiation, altered gravity, isolation, confined environments and distance from Earth. The main benefit of AstroHealth is that it presents multiple health indicators in one accessible interface. It helps users recognise unusual readings, understand potential risks and view suggested responses. Its intended impact is to support astronaut health awareness and encourage timely attention to possible health concerns, especially during missions where immediate medical assistance is limited. The application was developed using Kotlin, HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Android WebView used to display the web-based dashboard within the Android application. Antigravity and Gemini were used as development assistance tools. The creative aspect of AstroHealth is its combination of personal health monitoring, spaceflight risk awareness, alert generation and countermeasure guidance in one platform. During development, we considered the unique conditions of space missions, the importance of clear health information, ease of navigation, readability and the need to communicate potential risks without overwhelming the user. AstroHealth is currently a prototype that uses simulated health readings. It does not connect to actual astronaut sensors or provide real-time NASA telemetry. It demonstrates how an integrated health-monitoring interface could be developed and expanded for future space missions.
